text:
Maya: Quick convo: thinking about a "safety-budget" slider in the rollout fallback panel that ties a % of monthly budget to auto-degrades. Mock attached. Thoughts?
Alex: Interesting. Is this for cost-capped automatic fallbacks, or to sacrifice quality to save spend? Need clear wording.
Sam: Both. The idea: operator picks "safety budget" = how much token spend we're willing to let fallbacks consume this window before blocking further failovers. Prevents runaway redirects on noisy signals.
Leia: UX: show an SLO vs spend chart next to slider. X-axis = expected error reduction, Y-axis = estimated monthly token delta. Let operators preview three scenarios (low/med/high).
Tomas: Telemetry: emit `fallback_budget_decision` event with fields: decision_id, route, actor, budget_pct, estimated_tokens, projected_cost_usd, active_until. Also attach `X-Fallback-Decision` header when applied for joining.
Jin: Naming debate: call it "safety budget" or "fallback budget"? "Safety budget" sounds broader and might confuse with SLO budgets.
Maya: Good call. Maybe "fallback safety budget" or label: "Auto-fallback spend cap" (short).
Alex: API naming suggestion: in policy API use `fallback_policy.safety_budget_pct` and keep a separate `fallback_policy.action_sequence`. Avoid overloading term "budget" elsewhere.
Sam: Behaviors: when cap reached we should decline new auto-fallbacks and notify operator inbox. Also surface which decisions consumed the budget with a waterfall chart.
Leia: Important: retention + audits. Keep decision records 120d for billing teams. Exportable with estimated cost per-decision. Redact PII in any sampled payloads.
Tomas: Implementation note: we should compute estimated_tokens per-decision based on recent token-per-request sliding window for that route. Put a conservative multiplier (95th perc) to avoid underestimates.
Jin: What about multi-route budgets? Some customers want org-level pool vs route-level caps. Support hierarchical budgeting in UI?
Maya: Yes. Show toggles: [route-only] or [org-pool]. If org-pool selected, show remaining pool and contributors.
Alex: Rollout UX: when operator drags slider, show a confidence band and an "apply dry-run" button that runs a shadow simulation for 30s and shows real token usage.
Sam: Safety circuit: if errors spike after a fallback and cost keeps increasing, auto-escalate to restrict further fallbacks and page the oncall. We need hysteresis and cooldown.
Leia: RBAC: only org-admins can modify org-pool caps. Route-level caps editable by team leads. Log free-text reason for cap changes.
Tomas: Telemetry: add `budget_consumption_trace_sample=true` on sampled requests to join request traces to decisions. Configurable sampling rate per-org.
Maya: UX microcopy: avoid heavy words. Use "Spend cap for automatic rollbacks" with a tooltip that explains token vs USD. Show est. USD for customers not used to token metrics.
Jin: API compatibility: add new field to v2 policy: `safety_budget { type: "percent" | "tokens"; value: <int>; scope: "route" | "org" }`. That covers both token and percent inputs.
Alex: +1. Also debate: call the UI mode "shadow-simulate" or "simulate"? Shadow-simulate is explicit that it's a no-impact shadow. I prefer "simulate (shadow)" in UI.
Maya: Sounds good. I'll update the mock to include the slider, waterfall breakdown, and dry-run control.
Sam: I'll draft the operator inbox behavior: when pool is exhausted, create a high-priority inbox item with suggested manual actions.
Leia: I'll write the retention + export spec including redaction rules and approval workflow for org-level cap changes.
Tomas: I'll draft the telemetry proto and sample BigQuery mapping and include decision_id join example.
deploy-bot: deploybot: canary roll complete (sha=7f8c22) no fallback triggers in canary
Maya: Thanks all  I'll push updated figma and a short RFC.
Alex: :thumbsup:
